findings.title: Missing mango account check
findings.description: The Mango on-chain observer in the marginfi protocol does not verify whether the provided Mango accounts are actually associated with the user's marginfi account. This lack of validation allows an attacker to pass arbitrary Mango accounts during interactions with the protocol. The root cause is the absence of a constraint check ensuring that the mango_account_ai key matches the expected address from utp_config. An attacker can exploit this by invoking UtpMangoDeposit with a high-equity Mango account to gain an under-collateralized loan, or by invoking Liquidate with a low-equity account to unfairly liquidate a healthy position. The impact is critical, as it can lead to direct loss of funds from the protocol or other users due to improper margin enforcement and liquidation mechanics.

findings.title: Premature UTP deactivation
findings.description: The DeactivateUTP instruction considers a Mango UTP account empty if its asset value is below a 1 USD dust threshold, and allows deactivation even when non-zero assets remain. The root cause is the is_empty function relying solely on a fixed threshold without ensuring full withdrawal of funds prior to deactivation. An attacker can exploit this by depositing a small amount below the threshold, then deactivating the UTP to trigger self-liquidation, where the residual funds are effectively abandoned and absorbed by the protocol's insurance fund. The impact is low, as the loss per exploit is limited to dust amounts, but it represents a fund leakage vector over time and undermines proper accounting.
